activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today I am going to explain a routine but essential procedure that you regularly practise in the Electrical Technology workshop.
This procedure is a distribution board inspection.
Although it is routine, it must be done carefully and in the correct order, because faults in distribution boards can cause serious electrical hazards.
First, you have to isolate the power supply to the distribution board, because live circuits can cause electric shock.
Before any inspection begins, the board should be completely de-energised and clearly identified.
Then, you have to confirm isolation using a voltage tester so that you are sure the board is safe to work on.
After that, you have to wear insulated gloves and suitable safety equipment to reduce the risk of injury.
Next, you have to open the distribution board cover carefully to access internal components.
You don’t have to remove all breakers at this stage, because the inspection focuses only on visible connections and general conditions.
Once the board is accessible, you have to inspect terminals and cable connections carefully, because loose connections can lead to overheating.
Then, you have to check breakers for signs of damage or discolouration so that faulty components can be identified early.
After that, you have to tighten any loose terminals to ensure reliable electrical contact.
You also have to check earthing connections to confirm overall system safety.
You shouldn’t replace components immediately during this inspection, because defective parts are reported for scheduled maintenance.
This structured approach helps prevent electrical faults and unexpected failures.
Finally, you have to close the distribution board securely to protect internal components from dust and contact.
Then, you have to restore the power supply gradually so that the system can be observed safely.
After that, you have to monitor the board briefly to confirm normal operation.
You also have to clean the work area to maintain workshop standards.
You don’t have to carry out load testing at this stage, because the session focuses only on inspection procedures.
Following this sequence ensures electrical safety, system reliability, and correct maintenance practice.
